reason: The text consistently portrays leaders—God, Moses, Aaron, and Pharaoh—as the exclusive agents making decisions and taking meaningful actions. Non-leaders (Egyptian people, servants, animals, and Israelites) are depicted as passive recipients of consequences. The only exception is the Egyptian magicians (חרטומים), who attempt action but are ultimately ineffectual ('could not stand before Moses'). Their failed attempt to exercise agency actually reinforces the pattern rather than contradicting it, since their efforts prove futile while those of the leadership figures (especially Moses and God) succeed completely.
